faqs.question: Which businesses are legally required to undergo a Statutory Audit in India?
faqs.answer: Under Section 139 of the Companies Act, 2013, every incorporated company (Private Limited, Public Limited, or One Person Company) must appoint an independent statutory auditor and have its annual accounts audited, regardless of turnover or capital. For non-corporate entities (proprietorships, firms, LLPs), audit requirements are triggered by turnover thresholds under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
faqs.statuteReference: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 139; Income Tax Act, 1961 — Section 44AB

faqs.question: What are the turnover limits for a Tax Audit under Section 44AB?
faqs.answer: For businesses carrying on business operations, Tax Audit under Section 44AB is generally mandatory if total sales, turnover, or gross receipts exceed ₹1 Crore in the financial year. However, if cash receipts and cash payments do not exceed 5% of aggregate transactions (digital transaction incentive), the turnover threshold is increased to ₹10 Crores. For professionals, the threshold is ₹50 Lakhs gross receipts.
faqs.statuteReference: Income Tax Act, 1961 — Section 44AB & Budget amendments

faqs.question: When is GST Annual Return (GSTR-9) and Reconciliation (GSTR-9C) mandatory?
faqs.answer: GSTR-9 is mandatory for registered regular taxpayers whose aggregate annual turnover exceeds ₹2 Crores. The self-certified reconciliation statement in Form GSTR-9C is mandatory for taxpayers whose aggregate turnover exceeds ₹5 Crores in the financial year.

faqs.question: Why do real estate developers require CA Certificates under RERA?
faqs.answer: Under Section 4(2)(l)(D) of RERA 2016, 70% of amounts realized for real estate projects must be deposited in a scheduled bank separate account (Escrow). Withdrawals require three certificates: from the Project Engineer, Architect, and a Practicing Chartered Accountant (Form 3) certifying that withdrawal is in proportion to the percentage of project completion.
faqs.statuteReference: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 — Section 4(2)(l)(D)
